A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OATS research work. Their complete 26-page documents, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model accuracy and perplexity experiments, vision-transformer evaluations, CPU benchmarks, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a 256-token CPU throughput experiment in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The outlier scaling, alternating sparse and low-rank decomposition, sparsity options, parameter formulas, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The CPU additions introduce no algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The language and vision datasets and tasks are retained, including the appendix Qwen evaluation. The CPU changes vary sequence length within the existing inference-throughput benchmark without introducing a different task or data domain.

E2.justification: SparseGPT, Wanda, and DSNoT retain their participation in the corresponding accuracy comparisons. The new CPU experiment uses the existing Dense and Unstructured Pruning comparators; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 changes the reported CPU workload from a single batch of 2,048 tokens to a single token while retaining Table 7's numbers. Appendix A.6 adds a 256-token protocol using the same model, engine, and CPU. This establishes a reported setting revision, but does not establish that Table 7's experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.6 checks whether the CPU advantage persists at a higher token count, adding a limited workload-sensitivity analysis. Existing scaling, threshold-order, rank-ratio, iteration, and attention-rollout analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The additional CPU table follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 14 reports identical throughput for OATS and unstructured pruning at 256 tokens: 0.40, 0.43, and 0.49 tokens/second at 30%, 40%, and 50% compression, respectively, versus 0.37 for Dense. Existing numerical results remain unchanged. Table 7's revised workload description prevents interpreting the two versions as a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: The optimization problems, thresholding definitions, compression and rank formulas, and Appendix A.2 complexity analysis are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about retraining-free compression, predictive performance, sparse/low-rank interpretation, and CPU acceleration, including the abstract's up-to-1.37× advantage. These headline claims are not rewritten around the new workload-dependent evidence.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly acknowledges comparable CPU speedups for OATS and unstructured pruning at 256 tokens. It presents further acceleration as a prospective benefit of optimizations exploiting the sparse-plus-low-rank structure, adding a qualification absent from v2.

D1.justification: The CPU benchmarking documentation specifies a single-token workload for Table 7 and documents the new 256-token experiment's reuse of the Intel Xeon Gold 6148, 2.40 GHz, 32-core setup. Code links, pruning implementation details, and other hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix A.1, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to Wanda, robust PCA, and other sparse/low-rank compression approaches.

P1.justification: v3 makes a localized revision to the CPU paragraph, inserts Appendix A.6 and its discussion, and renumbers subsequent appendix sections and cross-references. The broader narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds CPU Table 14 and reflows appendix pages 21–22 to accommodate it. Existing later tables are renumbered and some are repositioned; their contents and all figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a more informative account of CPU efficiency by identifying Table 7 as single-token inference and adding the 256-token result showing no advantage over unstructured pruning. This improves transparency about workload dependence. The benefit is limited because the headline acceleration claims remain broadly worded, and the changed workload description accompanying unchanged Table 7 numbers is not explained.
